title: Use fixed points to obstruct affine-supported norm images
summary: A short symmetry-plus-support certificate can prune decomposition searches before any coefficient or phase search.
content: Let T be a binary-linear order-three action on labels, with amplitude field of characteristic three. Every nonempty invariant binary-affine support contains a fixed point: x+Tx+T^2x remains in the affine support and is fixed. But the image of I+T+T^2 is invariant and vanishes on fixed labels. Therefore that image contains no nonzero vector whose support is binary affine. The same reasoning excludes the project's norm-plus-one-affine-atom construction, even for an arbitrary seed.
whenToUse: A short symmetry-plus-support certificate can prune decomposition searches before any coefficient or phase search.
limitations: Sums of two residual atoms may not have affine support. Multiple norm packets require a common nonzero direction for this argument. Do not confuse symmetry of an output with symmetry of each input seed.
